One CreditSimulation document. The root carries the Risk block as typed
columns and owns the entities that migrate; the matrices are shared by name,
so they are their own table and an entity points at one.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One entity in the credit portfolio model: its name, its factor loadings,
the matrix it migrates on and the state it starts in. ORE refers to the
matrix by name in a text attribute; here the reference is a foreign key, so
renaming a matrix cannot silently orphan an entity.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A matrix is a named, reusable definition. ORE declares the states it spans
through the t0 and t1 attributes of its Data element, and the
probabilities as a square grid of text; the states and the probabilities
are held as rows in credit_simulation_matrix_cell_config, so this table
carries the name an entity refers to and nothing that can be derived.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Credit Simulation Matrix Row Config Table
ORE lays a transition matrix out on a fixed rating scale: every document in
the corpus is 8x8 and names the same eight ratings in the same order. Because
the scale is a property of the domain rather than data a user enters, it is
encoded in the type rather than seeded as rows: one row per source rating,
with one probability column per target rating. A matrix is therefore eight
rows, and a row reads the way the matrix is written in the document.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
Credit Simulation Netting Set Config Table
ORE writes the netting sets a credit simulation covers as a comma separated
list of codes inside one NettingSetIds element, which is a list stored as
text. A list is rows, so each code is a row here, keyed to the configuration
and carrying its position so the order is reproduced on export.
The codes name netting sets that the trading component owns; no netting set
entity exists yet, so the code is held as text until one does.

Classification of products at the granularity needed by the pricing engine to select the correct model and numerical method (e.g. EuropeanSwaption, BermudanSwaption, CMS).

The pricing methods that a pricing engine configuration names. ORE calls them engines. The name pricing_method keeps the table apart from the pricing engine configurations of the screens. Each row has a one-line description and a paragraph of detail, which the screens show next to the engine choice.

The vocabulary the pricing engine screens read. Each row says that a model and an engine price one pricing engine type, and marks the pair that ORE's examples use. The set of models and the set of engines are the distinct values of the model and engine columns.

Stores model parameters, engine parameters, and global parameters as normalised rows
for granular diffing. Product-scoped parameters have pricing_model_product_id set;
global parameters have it NULL with parameter_scope = 'global'.

numerical engine (e.g. Grid, AMC). Product-specific parameters are stored in

The pricing models that a pricing engine configuration names, with a one-line description and a paragraph of detail. The pricing engine screens show the detail next to the model choice. ORE calls the numerical or analytic method that prices with a model the engine, and the table pricing_method holds those.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The settings a pair of model and engine takes. The table states which settings a
pair accepts, the value ORE's examples use and whether ORE needs the setting. The
control the screen draws and the values it accepts belong to the value set of the
so the same rule serves every pair that takes the setting and the write path
that refuses a value outside it.

To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A sensitivity template key names an asset class, and the class is the reference
data's: interest_rates, fx, equity, commodity or credit. The key spells
that class as a short prefix a person recognises -- IR, FX, EQ, COMM,
CR -- and the two spellings are not the same, because ORE's template keys grew
their own vocabulary (it spells commodity COMM where the rest of ORE spells it
So this table is the bridge. It holds one row per class ORE presents a template
prefix for: the reference data code the template points at, the prefix the key
spells, and the words a person reads. Bond and inflation are asset classes of the
reference data with no row here, because ORE's examples present no template prefix
for them; a tenant that needs one adds the row.
The prefix is a presentation and never the identity: a key's spelling is the
tenant's, ORE resolves the key a configuration states, and the template's
asset_class_code is what the table checks. A screen that shows the class shows
the name from here, and the prefix stands beside it as what the key spells.
The rows are seeded for the system tenant and read by every tenant.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A sensitivity template key spells how its products are priced, in one of the five
forms ORE defines: Analytical, Semianalytical, FD, MC and Trade. The key
and a person reads the name beside it.
The method decides whether a template has an asset class at all. Four of the five
are a way of pricing a class of product, so a template that states one states the
class too. Trade is the exception: a trade-level template is the one ORE defines
without a class, because the sensitivities come from the trade itself rather than
from shifting a class of market data. needs_asset_class states that, and the
screen reads it rather than repeating the exception.
The methods are seeded for the system tenant and read by every tenant, so a
template that names a method ORE does not have is refused.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A sensitivity template is a key. The pricing engine configuration puts it on a
product with the setting SensitivityTemplate, and the sensitivity configuration
gives shift sizes and shift schemes to the products that carry the key. So the
row states the class of product the key belongs to and the method it is priced
by, and both are lookups: the class is the reference data's asset class, and the
method is one of the five ORE defines.
The class is the product's class and not a claim about which market keys the
shifts reach. A key may set shifts on keys outside its own class, which is the
sensitivity configuration's business and not this table's, so nothing here links
a template to the keys it reaches.
The method is the token a key spells
words a person reads. Four of the five methods price a class of product and
state it; the trade-level method is the one ORE defines without a class, so a
template that states it states no class, and the table checks that.
The key's spelling is the tenant's. ORE resolves a template key by looking up the
key the sensitivity configuration states, and a configuration may state a key
that ORE's own list does not hold, so a tenant can add a key of its own. The
table therefore holds every row to the metadata it states and does not hold the
key to a shape built out of asset_class_code and method_code.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
ORE applies a shift to a market point in one of three ways, which its schema
fixes as the shiftType enumeration in ore_types.xsd: Relative,
Absolute and EqualTo. Stress and sensitivity scenarios both use it.
The shift type is a seeded lookup, seeded for the system tenant and read by
every tenant, so a shift that names a type ORE does not have is refused.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A stress scenario in stresstest.xml is a set of shifts, grouped by the
element that holds them: DiscountCurves, FxSpots, SwaptionVolatilities
and thirteen more. The schema fixes the set as the children of its stresstest
type, apart from Date. Sixteen families in all.
The family is a seeded lookup, seeded for the system tenant and read by every
tenant, so a shift that names a family ORE does not have is refused.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
The root of an ORE stress document: StressTesting in stresstest.xml, which
holds the scenarios a run may apply and the one setting that governs how they
are applied. Twenty documents ship, holding forty-six scenarios between them.
Each row is one document. The scenarios hang off it, because a scenario is only
meaningful inside the library that names it.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One StressTest element of an ORE stress document. The id attribute is the
scenario's name, which is what a run's analytic refers to; the corpus holds
twenty-six distinct names across forty-six uses, so a name is shared between
What a scenario actually does lives in its shift blocks -- DiscountCurves,
FxSpots, SwaptionVolatilities and fifteen more -- and each is modelled as it
lands. This row holds the scenario itself: its name, the library it belongs to
and the date it is applied at.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One entry of one shift block of a stress scenario: a market object, the kind of
shift applied to it, and the shift itself. The corpus uses fourteen of the
eighteen families the schema allows -- DiscountCurves, IndexCurves, FxSpots,
FxVolatilities, SwaptionVolatilities, CapFloorVolatilities and the rest -- in
The families look different and are the same shape: an object named by one
ShiftType, and the shift as parallel lists of values and of tenors or
expiries. Fourteen tables would be fourteen copies of those five columns with
different attribute names. One table holds them all, with the family as a
column and the object's name in object_key, which is what makes adding a
family a seeded value rather than a table.
The entries carry a few things besides the shift -- ShiftSize, IRCurves,
ShiftTerms -- and those are written into extras as a stated list of
name and value pairs, because they differ from family to family and none is
Each row belongs to exactly one scenario, in the order the document wrote it.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
A todaysmarket.xml document is a set of collections of twenty-four kinds --
YieldCurves, DiscountingCurves, FxSpots and the rest -- plus
configurations that pick one collection of each kind. The schema fixes the set
as the children of its TodaysMarket element, apart from Configuration, and
fixes for each kind the element its entries are written as and the attribute
or two attributes an entry identifies itself by.
The kind is a seeded lookup, seeded for the system tenant and read by every
tenant, so a collection or a binding that names a kind ORE does not have is
refused, and an entry no longer repeats its kind's key attribute.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One collection — DiscountingCurves, FxSpots, SwaptionVolatilities and the
rest. A document writes up to twenty-four of them, each optional, each holding
its own ordered list of entries.
A document may write the same kind more than once under different ids, for
example a DiscountingCurves with id default and another with id inccy. A
Configuration selects one of them by that id. So the collection is a thing
with an identity, an order and its own entries, and it has a table. Almost every
An entry points at its collection rather than repeating the collection's name.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One ORE todaysmarket.xml document, held as the thing the collections and the
configurations hang off. The document itself carries no market data: it is an
ordered set of collections, each entry naming a curve by reference, plus named
configurations that select one collection of each kind by the collection's id.
The entries live on todays_market_entry, the configurations on
todays_market_configuration, and the references a configuration makes on
todays_market_configuration_binding. This row is only the identity of the
document, so that a tenant may hold more than one and a report may choose
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One reference a configuration makes. A Configuration block writes up to
twenty-four of these. Each names a collection kind and the id of one collection
of that kind: DiscountingCurvesId inccy selects the DiscountingCurves
The reference is text, not a foreign key to todays_market_collection. ORE
resolves it by name when it builds the market, and the export only has to write
it back. Whether it should become a real key is left to the work that first
resolves it, which is producing the engine input from the entities.
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One Configuration block. It is not a collection of entries: it is a bundle of
references, each naming one entry of one collection, so that a report can select
a coherent set of curves and volatilities by name instead of restating them.
It identifies itself by a required id attribute, which is unique within a
document. The references it makes live on
AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One entry of one collection. Twenty-three of the document's twenty-four
collections are this shape: an entry identifying itself by one attribute and
carrying a reference as its text, in a position.
The attribute is not one name. It is name for nineteen collections,
currency for DiscountingCurves, pair for the two FX collections and the
literal string key for SwaptionVolatilities and CapFloorVolatilities.
Which one is a fact about the collection's kind, so it is held once on
todays_market_collection_kind rather than repeated on every entry.
SwaptionVolatilities and CapFloorVolatilities identify by two attributes at
once, so key_value_2 carries the second. SwapIndexCurves is the only
collection whose entry nests, and discounting carries its one child.
Index and the other groups: ores_schema.puml
